How Word Tile Rush scoring works

In current Word Tile Rush, each accepted word scores one point per letter; the 90-second run uses a fixed local word list and no saved best score.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 15, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Spell words. Clear the grid.

Play Word Tile RushBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: Current Word Tile Rush adds one point for each letter in an accepted word. A five-letter word earns five points—not a length-squared bonus.

Score by accepted word length

The game checks the selected path against its built-in word set. If the word is accepted, the score increases by the number of letters in that path: a three-letter word earns 3 points, a four-letter word earns 4, and a six-letter word earns 6. A path that is not in the local list clears without adding points.

The path must use neighboring cells, including diagonals, and cannot reuse a tile as a new step. The current control allows a selection to be shortened by returning to an earlier tile. The on-screen Submit word button is available after a path of at least three letters.

Points are only one part of the run

The game begins with 90 seconds when the first tile is selected. A valid word clears its letters, lets each column settle downward, and inserts a new row at the bottom. A run ends when the timer reaches zero or the top row is occupied after an accepted word.

A longer accepted word earns more points than a shorter accepted word, but it is not multiplied or squared. Use the current board and timer to decide whether a visible word is worth submitting; there is no saved best score or leaderboard.

For the grid’s rise and column behavior, read Managing a rising word-game grid. The current game page lists its controls and local word set.
